merger_description:
Investment funds advised, managed or owned by Global Infrastructure Management (**GIM**), EQT AB (**EQT**) and the Qatar Investment Authority (**QIA**) propose to acquire The AES Corporation (**AES Corporation**) (the **Acquisition**). Following the Acquisition, AES Corporation will be jointly controlled by GIM and EQT. GIM is owned by BlackRock.

  

GIM, EQT and QIA’s interests in Australia include:  

• Akaysha (interest owned by a connected entity of GIM): a renewable energy developer specialising in large-scale battery energy storage systems.  

• Nebras Power (interest owned by QIA): owns interests in large-scale renewable energy generation assets, including in Australia.   

• OX2 (interest owned by EQT): a developer of large-scale wind, solar and energy storage projects.  

• Recurrent (interest owned by a connected entity of GIM): a global developer, owner and operator of large-scale solar and energy storage projects.  

• Vena Energy (interest owned by GIM): a renewable energy power producer with solar, wind and battery storage assets in the Asia-Pacific region.

  

AES Corporation is a publicly listed company, headquartered in Arlington, Virginia, United States. AES Corporation, through its subsidiaries, owns and operates a global portfolio of power plants and utility systems that generate, transmit, distribute and sell electricity to wholesale and retail customers across residential, commercial, industrial and governmental sectors. Its generation mix spans coal, natural gas, hydro, wind, solar and energy storage systems. AES Corporation operates in Australia through its interests in 5B Holdings Pty Ltd (**5B**) which primarily manufactures prefabricated solar infrastructure and Fluence Energy Pty Ltd (**Fluence**) which supplies energy storage products, software and related services.

determination_table_content.details:
Investment funds advised, managed or owned by Global
Infrastructure Management (GIM), EQT AB (EQT) and the Qatar
Investment Authority (QIA)’s proposed acquisition of 100% of the
share capital in The AES Corporation (AES Corporation)
(the Acquisition). Following the Acquisition, AES Corporation would
be jointly controlled by GIM and EQT.

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABZE(1) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition may be put into effect.

The acquirers, GIM, EQT and QIA, are institutional investors. They
have the following relevant interests in Australia:
▪ Businesses in which GIM or a connected entity of GIM has an
interest:
o Akaysha, a renewable energy developer specialising
in large-scale battery energy storage system
o Recurrent, a global developer, owner and operator of
large-scale solar and energy storage projects
o Vena Energy, a renewable energy power producer
with solar, wind and battery storage assets in the
Asia-Pacific region
o Nxzen, a technology and engineering consultant
specialising in the energy, utilities, and infrastructure
sectors.
▪ Businesses in which EQT or a connected entity of EQT has an
Interest:
o OX2, a developer of large-scale wind, solar and
energy storage projects.
▪ Businesses in which QIA or a connected entity of QIA has an
interest:
o Endeavour Energy, a New South Wales electricity
distribution network
o Nebras Power, owns interests in large-scale
renewable energy generation assets, including in
Australia.
The target, AES Corporation, owns and operates a global portfolio of
power plants and utility systems that generate, transmit, distribute
and sell electricity to wholesale and retail customers across
residential, commercial, industrial and governmental sectors. AES
Corporation operates in Australia through its interests in:
▪ 5B, which primarily manufactures prefabricated solar
infrastructure
▪ Fluence Energy, which supplies energy storage products,
software and related services.

GIM, EQT and QIA’s interests in Australian electricity generation,
transmission and distribution in some cases overlap and/or have a
between the Parties vertical relationship with AES Corporation’s Australian operations (or
the operations of a business in which AES Corporation has an
interest) in solar energy and energy storage system product
manufacturing, delivery and the provision of related services.

When making a determination in Phase 1, the Australian Competition
and Consumer Commission (ACCC) undertakes a competition
assessment and considers whether it is appropriate for an
acquisition to be approved or subject to further assessment in
Phase 2 in accordance with section 51ABZJ of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act). In doing so, the ACCC must have
regard to the object of the Act and all relevant matters, including the
interests of consumers.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notified acquisitions, see the ACCC’s merger assessment guidelines
and interim merger process guidelines.
In conducting its competition assessment, the ACCC has considered
the information and documents that were submitted with the
notification form and publicly available information.
The ACCC has determined that the Acquisition may be put into
effect as it considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to have the
effect of substantially lessening competition in any market. In
reaching its decision, and based on the material before it, the ACCC
makes the following findings.
• there is limited overlap between GIM, EQT and QIA’s interests
and the AES Corporation’s interests in Australia.
• the merged entity would likely continue to face competition from
alternative suppliers of solar farms & solutions and battery
energy storage system products.
• the merged entity would be unlikely to have the ability and
incentive to foreclose rival battery energy storage system
operators’ access to battery energy storage system products
and related services due to the availability of alternative
suppliers, such as, CATL, CSI Solar, GE Vernova, Goldwind,
Sungrow, Tesla and Wartsila.

A notifying party, or other person who has been allowed to do so by
the Australian Competition Tribunal, may apply for review if they are
dissatisfied with the determination. Pursuant to section 100C of the
Act, applications for review of the determination are to be made to
the Australian Competition Tribunal before the end of 14 calendar
days after this statement of reasons was included on the ACCC’s
Acquisitions Register. To confirm whether there has been any
application for review, please contact the Australian Competition
Tribunal.
